newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn-KfW to place Lufthansa stake in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Bonn-KfW to place Lufthansa stake in autumn.

text.p: Germany's transport ministry said on Thursday that the German government's remaining stake in airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG would be sold in the autumn through the government development agency KfW.
The KfW would also sell a 1.77 percent stake in the airline, which it has held for some time, in the flotation.
The issue volume will be five billion marks, based on current share valuations, the ministry said in a statement.

Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and SBC Warburg would act as global coordinators of the Lufthansa sale, Germany's second-biggest initial public offering (IPO) to date, the transport ministry, the finance ministry and the KfW said in a joint statement.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell will act as senior co-lead manager, with DG Bank and Merrill Lynch as co-lead managers.

The composition of the consortium should ensure that at least fifty percent of the shares should remain in German hands, the ministry said. This would be achieved by making Germany the main focus of the share placement.

"With special consideration for German investors, this should strengthen Germany as a financial centre and help develop an equity culture in Germany following the positive experiences of the Deutsche Telekom IPO," the statement said.
